whole_site_assembly_blocker.why: assemble_production_site._partition_path resolves a market's partition by an explicit named table first and a glob second; the glob strips the last id segment, so for raleigh-nc it looks for raleigh_final_partition_*.json while the committed, contract-conformant file is raleigh_nc_final_partition_007.json. final_partition_present reads False, the market is NOT ASSEMBLABLE, no raleigh-nc fragment is built, and a candidate staged with Raleigh participating fails global.launch_participation_agrees_with_source (the assembler's own Nashville comment records the identical trap). The modern registration lane never hits this: market_package_writer falls back to the <us>_final_partition_*.json glob, so the sealed package, FAST rule J and the release-index candidate all resolved the partition.
whole_site_assembly_blocker.how_every_prior_market_resolved_it: one named entry in assemble_production_site._partition_path (Toledo, Lexington, Nashville, Charlotte each added theirs in their launch-prep order)
whole_site_assembly_blocker.why_not_done_here: The order forbids editing factory code, forbids running a broad regression, and says STOP if one is requested. A data-only rename of the partition to the glob's spelling was rejected because the registration contract's final_partition role is <us>_final_partition_*.json and the market-local helper writes that name; the rename would be UNKNOWN to the composite proof.
